{
  "key": "compat-test-001",

  "structure": {
    "organizing-axis": {
      "id": "stage-gated-pipeline",
      "name": "Stage Gated Pipeline",
      "tier": "organizing-axis",
      "modes": [
        "operate",
        "analyze"
      ],
      "thesis": "The surface is organized by the ordered stages an object must pass through, with blocked transitions treated as the central problem.",
      "refuses": "It rejects a flat inventory that erases sequence, handoffs, and the conditions required to advance.",
      "laws": {
        "grouping": "Create one zone per real lifecycle stage in process order. Place each object only in its current stage, and isolate blocked objects within that stage rather than inventing a separate object type.",
        "hierarchy": "The stage constraining total flow earns the focal position. Total throughput may support it, but a vanity completion count may never displace the active bottleneck.",
        "actions": "Stage transitions live on the object or selected cohort and name the resulting state. Process configuration and bulk exceptions live outside the primary flow.",
        "empty": "An empty stage means either healthy flow, no arrivals, or a broken upstream handoff. The state must identify which interpretation applies and show the relevant interval.",
        "motion": "Only objects advancing, returning, or becoming blocked may move between stages. Decorative movement along the pipeline is forbidden. When reduced motion is requested, make the state change immediate and retain the same status information."
      },
      "fits": [
        "sales opportunity pipeline",
        "content approval workflow",
        "order fulfillment console"
      ],
      "avoid": "Avoid when stages are optional, cyclic, or disputed enough that a linear progression would misrepresent the work.",
      "rating": 3
    },
    "depth-strategy": {
      "id": "progressive-reveal",
      "name": "Progressive Reveal",
      "tier": "depth-strategy",
      "modes": [
        "read",
        "persuade",
        "operate",
        "analyze",
        "experience"
      ],
      "thesis": "The surface exposes the minimum complete answer first, then reveals supporting complexity at the exact point a reader asks for it.",
      "refuses": "It rejects both indiscriminate expansion and teaser summaries that withhold information required for the primary decision.",
      "laws": {
        "grouping": "Keep each primary answer with a labeled disclosure of its explanation, evidence, or advanced options. Disclosure depth may not exceed two levels for routinely needed content.",
        "hierarchy": "The complete first-order answer earns the focal position. Chevrons, collapsed counts, and hidden technical detail may never compete with it.",
        "actions": "Reveal actions state what will appear and, where useful, how much. Task-changing actions do not masquerade as disclosure and must navigate explicitly.",
        "empty": "A disclosure with no additional content is removed. A primary empty state explains the zero condition before offering optional guidance.",
        "motion": "Only the requested region expands or contracts, preserving the trigger and nearby reading position. When reduced motion is requested, make the state change immediate and retain the same status information."
      },
      "fits": [
        "technical documentation",
        "onboarding explanation",
        "complex settings guide"
      ],
      "avoid": "Avoid when hidden material is required for every decision, when users compare distant details, or when repeated expansion would become routine labor.",
      "rating": 2
    },
    "framing": {
      "id": "status-first",
      "name": "Status First",
      "tier": "framing",
      "modes": [
        "operate",
        "analyze"
      ],
      "thesis": "The surface opens with a direct judgment of current state against a declared target before explaining causes or offering detail.",
      "refuses": "It rejects opening with activity totals, navigation, or background context that delays the answer to whether things are okay.",
      "laws": {
        "grouping": "Lead with state versus target, then group causes, consequences, and responses in that order. Orientation remains present but visually quiet.",
        "hierarchy": "The current state judgment earns the single focal position. A raw metric may never hold it without a target, threshold, or prior basis.",
        "actions": "The primary action addresses the state shown and sits adjacent to it when immediate. Explanatory and administrative actions descend with the supporting zones.",
        "empty": "No measurable state means status is unknown, not healthy. The surface must identify the missing scope, freshness, or data source.",
        "motion": "Only a material state transition may move or change emphasis, according to a declared significance threshold. When reduced motion is requested, make the state change immediate and retain the same status information."
      },
      "fits": [
        "service health dashboard",
        "project status report",
        "account compliance page"
      ],
      "avoid": "Avoid when no trustworthy target exists or when the user's first question is which specific item needs work.",
      "rating": 3
    }
  },
  "direction": {
    "id": "admiralty-chart-5011",
    "name": "Admiralty Chart 5011",
    "source": "British Admiralty Chart 5011, Symbols and Abbreviations Used on Admiralty Charts, 1984 edition, International Chart hydrographic notation.",
    "strength": "composition",
    "verb": "instructs",
    "modes": [
      "analyze",
      "operate",
      "read"
    ],
    "thesis": "Safe action depends on distinguishing route, depth, obstruction, and uncertainty at a glance, so the interface becomes a navigational instrument rather than a pile of status widgets.",
    "laws": {
      "palette": "Chart white #F7F4E9 is the base, shallow-water cyan #B9E1E8 marks constrained depth, land buff #E7D4A2 marks fixed territory, magenta #B04691 carries route and notice overlays, black #151515 records soundings and hazards, and green #6E9B78 marks intertidal or drying areas.",
      "type": "Use a narrow chart sans with italic feature names, tiny tabular soundings, uppercase region labels, and abbreviation keys; semantic typography remains stable even when spatial scale changes.",
      "topology": "Build a continuous operating field, show channels and exclusion areas directly in it, keep the symbol key in a docked margin, and reserve inset panels for harbor-scale detail or procedure.",
      "controls": "Tools appear as symbol-key entries with icon, code, and label, selected routes use a magenta pecked line, hazards demand a black symbol plus text, and focus uses a white halo bounded by magenta.",
      "motion": "The current track may extend, tide or forecast overlays may advance, and warnings may appear at the affected coordinate; coastlines, hazard positions, and depth labels must never drift. When reduced motion is requested, replace this movement with an immediate state change that preserves the same information."
    },
    "spark": "A deployment planner lays release stages along a magenta recommended track, plots dependency hazards as black wreck symbols, and shades shallow capacity zones cyan before the operator commits.",
    "borrowSkeleton": "Take the operating field, route and hazard distinction, uncertainty notation, docked key, and coordinate-specific warnings; do not decorate cards with anchors or nautical stripes.",
    "rating": 2
  }
}
